result.markdown:
If you're looking at the original **Oz books by L. Frank Baum**, there are 14 novels, and a handful are generally considered the standouts. Interestingly, some of the later books are favorites among readers who grew up with the series.

Based on reader ratings, literary commentary, and fan interest, here's the shortlist I'd recommend.

## The best Wizard of Oz books

![A Digital Archive of 1,800+ Children's Books from UCLA |  Open Culture](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/ktPSnTMEmSElZshwWTzqxNKicoMxk-5To_TV0k5UX3P4DSE6dNbSFoI-NJBmZ-0p5qSvlZbxl1y7goSG2kkLHKti8J84mByOHTqDj56vSAraePGvb9H5AAOSl-p-KS9usgOu9FI-7V3OsiPiKAocGb8oW01oeyDic5Q38s9lu2jeUdAa-ma4vNIsqKyBzaDp?purpose=fullsize)

**1\. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz \(1900)**

(Essential classic)

The original and arguably the best. Introduces Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Tin Woodman, Cowardly Lion, and the magical world of Oz. More surprising and occasionally darker than the famous movie.

---

![Ozma of Oz: Record of Her Adventures with Dorothy Gale of Kansas, the Yellow Hen, the Scarecrow, the Tin Woodman, Tiktok, the Cowardly Lion and the Hungry Tiger; Besides Other Good People too Numerous to Mention Faithfully Recorded Herein by L. Frank Baum: Fair Hardcover | Reasons To Live Books](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/b4uqHO2aERnrzTXkUivYASpHWPO3YjpcCsnnsIZs59LdgF7zVOE_DN755uon0xFRojkMHxUS4UfIaWqXfyANOv-o9cArt5G62YnO9EIx4-Snh5jBv362VfysQaFJNphcBal0HPmHjgsSUZHqpV8DYhF2Qvs8O4bUcOEDVUo5oeZf3d4qXKukmBu8Y0B7XSf2?purpose=fullsize)

**2\. Ozma of Oz \(1907)**

(One of the fan favorites)

A particularly imaginative adventure featuring Princess Ozma, the Nome King, and the unforgettable mechanical man Tik-Tok. Often rated among Baum's very best.

---

![THE MARVELOUS LAND OF OZ
by Baum, L. Frank; Neill, John R |
1904 |
Reilly & Britton |
Biblio](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/sDL3NOOZ-vo8f-9C_-gE1EM9-bM0y35-oDubDa4N7XVJ9DW7NEgrlHYb1j_4Drh3r66jo69CnmIObKHvSlUYsHnai2KzmcWp5tEV3oxTUnCaDL4jlr-AWbkCWPIGN7f_ezDq97mFgnDfubP490r117lRselp_tvC11URrNl9ONVA4doNEQBhJX1DXqow7ox1?purpose=fullsize)

**3\. The Marvelous Land of Oz \(1904)**

Introduces Tip, Jack Pumpkinhead, the Woggle-Bug, and the origins of Ozma. A wonderfully eccentric sequel with a lot of humor.

---

![[Baum, L. Frank] Emerald City of Oz
by Baum, L. Frank |
[1910] |
Reilly & Britton |
Biblio](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/OJodjw_kD1NOGA_U9j9gI9yK2y2ncwaCQ5liv-RZr7d_IZZtdGoX0Pde9vX4JdMJOhYvFFMKeHVuo5a5wFlrirkBW4Gx2HrufX_kynQY5nH__mgQ282icALpc1-5Ki12fEW2yv6F3StYq1Q1gagyPNYTRwXefKCS-MWETvpewNW2cwl56bj3Wzs0WF-J-dc4?purpose=fullsize)

**4\. The Emerald City of Oz \(1910)**

Dorothy and her family settle in Oz. Particularly appealing if you love the world-building, history, and magical society of Oz.

---

![L. Frank Baum 'the Lost Princess Of Oz' Book](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/wfQXuyvY5zDcx0MTbm_iM_xzsU082hJimjN_qx9VhknRWXmjcC4pGdFN6lbMbcp6_RXp4F1GUPaasdtQ061uNOQE-ZR9wXz_bVN66R6ypbw9l_G9OEwf_y1Oa291A4FQyzlgx--CDXH3RlaL_tXFs1oWJRoAKuDMK18Y62OSte1pR9XDGi_JT1MyCvAqMVkv?purpose=fullsize)

**5\. The Lost Princess of Oz \(1917)**

A mystery-adventure involving the disappearance of Princess Ozma. One of the more enjoyable later entries.

---

![](https://images.openai.com/static-rsc-4/lSeU7s03YVJi_2zEF11nYSC-hRoCqMKZSwrhkUCGz4e2l-RdfimT6oh4yi8siVnVk20J9T5wQD6i5FIKDt6IFht_OJcoVtGH-wKHhS6Bfi2EXMSNj6DCyisGeFAD5FNjgyHr6JsiqZO-NYsTjKY0eZhI4TV5APu6mCteIfgMG4HnJCxnj751LoZZdWfPDZUx?purpose=fullsize)

**6\. The Patchwork Girl of Oz \(1913)**

Features Scraps, the Patchwork Girl, one of Baum's most memorable creations. Especially good if you enjoy the stranger, more whimsical side of Oz.

These selections are consistent with reader-rating patterns and critical discussion, although there isn't one universally accepted ranking. ## My recommended reading order

If you want to explore the series properly, I'd read Baum's original books in publication order\:

1. The Wonderful Wizard of Oz (1900)
2. The Marvelous Land of Oz (1904)
3. Ozma of Oz (1907)
4. Dorothy and the Wizard in Oz (1908)
5. The Road to Oz (1909)
6. The Emerald City of Oz (1910)
7. The Patchwork Girl of Oz (1913)
8. Tik-Tok of Oz (1914)
9. The Scarecrow of Oz (1915)
10. Rinkitink in Oz (1916)
11. The Lost Princess of Oz (1917)
12. The Tin Woodman of Oz (1918)
13. The Magic of Oz (1919)
14. Glinda of Oz (1920)

[www.fantasticfiction.com](https://www.fantasticfiction.com/b/l-frank-baum/oz/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.chipublib.org](https://www.chipublib.org/blogs/post/chicago-classics-the-oz-books/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

## What about books written by other authors?

There are also 26 additional books in the original publisher's famous forty-book Oz canon, written by authors who continued the series after Baum died.

One especially interesting author is Ruth Plumly Thompson\. Her books include\:

- The Royal Book of Oz \(1921)
- Kabumpo in Oz \(1922)
- The Cowardly Lion of Oz \(1923)

These are worth exploring if you become a serious Oz enthusiast. [www.thereadingorder.com](https://www.thereadingorder.com/the-wizard-of-oz-books-in-order/?utm_source=chatgpt.com)[www.cerealreaders.com](https://www.cerealreaders.com/series/246/oz-by-l-frank-baum?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

---

**My personal recommendation\:** Start with *The Wonderful Wizard of Oz*, *Ozma of Oz*, and *The Marvelous Land of Oz*\. Those three give you a wonderful sense of what makes Baum's imagination so special.

One question: Are you interested primarily in the **original classic children's fantasy**, or are you interested in the stranger, darker, more unusual Oz mythology that develops throughout the 40-book series? That distinction changes which books I'd recommend most.
